title: Vijñānabhairava
author: Anonymous (Trika tantra, attributed to the Rudrayāmala)
edition_cited: GRETIL e-text (data entry Marino Faliero, 1998), lightly corrected, IAST; supplied by the user
summary: Bhairava's 112 dhāraṇās. Several concern seen light and the visual field: closing the eyes and other openings with the hands until a bindu is seen (36); a fiery tilaka-like bindu (37); peacock-feather-coloured circles (32); fixing the gaze on space variegated by the brilliance of sun or lamp (76); unwavering gaze into clear sky (84); contemplating the darkness of a moonless night, or the black form before the closed eyes (87-88); simply holding the eyes motionless (113).
why_relevant: Classical Śaiva source of short gaze, darkness and eye-closure methods, one of which names a seen bindu.

date_evidence.basis: GRETIL e-text header (data entry 1998); the text itself is first-millennium
